title: DONKI · Solar flare archive
use: Real recorded flare classes and dates seed fictional Mars events. Flare class is not a Mars radiation forecast; dose scaling is a game rule. Data are archived, never live.

title: Curiosity RAD · Surface radiation
use: RAD measured an average 0.67 mSv/day at Gale Crater in August 2012–June 2013. The game’s 0–100 cumulative dose is a teaching scale, not a medical dose.

title: OSDR · OSD-658
use: OSD-658 found a radiation-dose-dependent DNA-repair response in Arabidopsis seedlings. This laboratory study informs our plant science log, not a claim about human risk or Mars crop yields.

title: MOXIE · Oxygen on Mars
use: Oxygen can be extracted from atmospheric carbon dioxide. Our ice melter is a separate, simplified water system.

title: Perseverance · Talking to Mars
use: 3–22 minute one-way delay. We use a fixed illustrative 12 minutes, shortened to 12 game seconds, rather than claiming current ephemeris data.

title: Opportunity · The 2018 dust storm
use: Dust and loss of sunlight threaten solar power. Item-tossing dust devils are a playful exaggeration: thin Mars air cannot throw heavy crates this way.

title: NASA · Growing in Mars soil
use: Perchlorates are harmful salts. Washing soil is an educational simplification, not a validated farming method.

title: Mars facts · NASA
use: A sol is roughly 24 hours 39 minutes. Mars has very thin air; nights are cold. Launch opportunities occur about every 26 months. The 15-sol return window is fictional, with a return vehicle already on Mars.

title: NASA · Radiation protection
use: Water and regolith can reduce exposure. Shield effectiveness depends on particle type, thickness, and secondary radiation; no shelter eliminates all exposure.
